title: Delmira Agustini's birth chart
metaDescription: Delmira Agustini's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 1.2° Scorpio. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Across the nine placements whose signs are settled, cardinal leads with four. Cardinal signs open the seasons, and a cardinal-heavy chart is read as one that starts things.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Scorpio, but precisely: 1.2°, first decan, 0°–10°, under Mars in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 17.6° Scorpio, Venus at 21.3° Libra, Mars at 13.7° Sagittarius. Mercury in a water sign reads as a mind that absorbs before it argues; Venus in an air sign reads as taste led by wit and proportion; Mars in a fire sign reads as drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Venus and Saturn hold the closest angle here — a square, 1.1° wide. Right angles are where the scheme puts its grit. A square asks two functions to work in a mode neither would have chosen. Behind it, Venus conjunction Jupiter at 1.8°, and Jupiter square Saturn at 2.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These angles were checked through every hour of that civil day and survive throughout, which is why an unrecorded hour does not disturb them.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Two planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. Venus in Libra at 21.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Cancer at 22.4° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements air 4, water 3, fire 1, earth 1; modalities cardinal 4, fixed 3, mutable 2. An air-weighted chart thinks in through-lines; the sentence is how it takes hold of the world. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Virgo into Libra during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.7° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
